title: Session lifecycle — checkpointlets sandbox
content:
Goal / elevator
- Explore a super-lightweight notion of ‘checkpointlets’ — tiny resumable context checkpoints that a client can ask to persist and later resume. Target: useful for mobile/web assistants and workflows where full session persistence is expensive or undesirable.

Problem statement
- Current session models are either: ephemeral (no resume) or heavy (full snapshot with all context + embeddings). Both extremes waste tokens or infrastructure.
- Use cases: short-lived composition tasks (writing drafts), multi-turn forms, agent tool-chains where intermediate state matters, user-swapped devices.
- Constraints: privacy (should be easy to redact), size (<= few KB per checkpointlet), fast restore (<100ms lookups), cheap storage (per small checkpoint pricing), and tolerant to partial loss.

Checkpointlet concept (rough)
- A checkpointlet = a small JSON payload that captures minimal state to resume a focused sub-journey. Think of it as a micro-snapshot: prompt prefix pointers + last-K turns (compressed), selected metadata (active tools, selected persona flags), and a compact provenance tag.
- Can be created by client (explicit save) or auto-sampled after certain actions (e.g., after toolchain completes).
- Restore semantics: model is fed a short reconstruction prompt assembled by server from checkpointlet metadata + optionally fetched content (e.g., up to 512 tokens). The runtime decides which model variant to use for resumption (cheap vs full).

High-level goals / success metrics
- UX: 80% of resume attempts should feel coherent to users in simple composition tasks (small user study).
- Perf: snapshot write < 50ms median (client->control plane), restore round-trip < 150ms median for hosted tier.
- Cost: incremental storage < $0.0008 per checkpointlet per month at 1M monthly checkpointlets.
- Reliability: system tolerates 1–5% checkpointlet loss without catastrophic UX failure (fallback: re-run short context from scratch).

User stories (examples)
- As a mobile user, I want to save my draft card so I can continue later on another device with minimal latency and minimal data sent.
- As a developer, I want an explicit API to create and list checkpointlets for a session so I can implement “save draft” and “restore draft” UX easily.
- As a compliance engineer, I want checkpointlets to be optionally stored encrypted and TTL-ed automatically.

APIs (sketch)
- POST /v1/sessions/{id}/checkpointlets {name, type, payload, ttl?} -> id, size
- GET /v1/sessions/{id}/checkpointlets -> list of metadata (id, name, created_at, preview)
- POST /v1/checkpointlets/{id}/restore {mode: preview|full|merge} -> restored_prompt_template
- DELETE /v1/checkpointlets/{id} -> 204

Client UX patterns
- Explicit save button -> creates checkpointlet with user-facing label (e.g., “saved note — Oct 2”).
- Auto-checkpoint after key events (tool success, form submit). Default off; product opt-in per app.
- Preview mode: fetch a 1–2 sentence preview assembled from checkpointlet metadata without paying for model tokens.

Storage & privacy notes
- Keep payloads small; encourage clients to store large attachments elsewhere and put pointers in checkpointlet.
- Encryption: default server-side encryption, optional customer-managed KMS for private deployments.
- Redaction: easy redact API to remove PII fields; retention TTL support.

Runtime & cost model ideas
- Tiered storage backends: hot (fast reads, short TTL) for recently active checkpointlets + cold (cheaper) for archival.
- Pricing: per-checkpointlet write + tiny monthly retention fee. Offer bundle credits in Dedicated.

Telemetry / metrics to capture
- checkpointlet.create.count, create.latency.p50/p95
- checkpointlet.restore.count, restore.latency.p50/p95
- checkpointlet.size.bytes.histogram
- resume-coherence-score (sampled human evals / automated similarity heuristics)
- restore-fallback-rate (how often restore fails and client falls back to full context)

Experiment plan (MVP)
- Phase 0 (proto): client-only format + local storage + server stub that saves JSON. Integrate with web demo. (2 weeks)
- Phase 1 (hosted POC): implement create/list/restore API, hot storage, simple preview endpoint, implement TTL + SSE events for change. Start 50 internal users. (4 weeks)
- Phase 2 (metrics + UX): instrument coherence evals, run 200 internal sessions, iterate on payload shape (how much history to include). (3 weeks)
- Phase 3 (private + encryption): KMS option + retention controls for enterprise. (3–4 weeks)

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How to formalize payload schema so we don’t lock clients but also keep server-side tooling useful? (versioned schema + validators?)
- Compression vs. semantic pointers — should we store compressed token sequences or only pointers + server-side reconstruct?
- Sync conflicts: two devices creating checkpointlets simultaneously — likely treat as separate checkpointlets, provide UI merge (out of scope for MVP).

Immediate next steps (for me)
- Draft API proto and minimal JSON schema; run by Sam and Rhea.
- Wire up a playground demo (static web page) to show create->list->restore UX.
- Add JIRA ticket INF-4827 with acceptance criteria and sample events.

Notes to self
- Keep naming tight: 'checkpointlet' as working term. If it sticks, create glossary entry in Confluence.
- Don’t over-index on full fidelity resumes in MVP; aim for “good enough” coherence for micro-tasks.
- Remember to check with security about encryption defaults for users in EU/regulated customers.

Random thoughts (brain dump)
- Could pair checkpointlets with a small vector fingerprint for deduping similar checkpoints across users (privacy implications).
- Consider quick-share links that auto-expire (share draft with collaborator for 24h).
- Potential productization: checkpointlet templates for onboarding flows (pre-fab mini-snapshots).

---
